messages:
eli: heads up — saw a p99 CPU spike on telemetry-exporter workers around 11:03 UTC. it lines up with a retention roll where span retention went from 7d -> 90d. any theories?

maya: :eyes: can you paste collector logs and the exporter metrics (p95/p99 per pod)?

eli: copying a small snippet from the exporter pod: 
```
[11:03:12] exporter_worker.go:217 CPU=92% spans_processed=1234567 batch_size=120 avg_span_size=980B
[11:03:13] exporter_worker.go:221 flush_time_ms=18 export_http_error=0
[11:03:14] exporter_worker.go:223 mem_rss=1.8GiB spans_in_queue=420k
```

eli: attached metrics: exporter_export_time_p99=480ms, exporter_process_cpu=88%, spans_in_last_min=2.4M

daria: hmm that's a lot of spans. two quick suspects: 1) retention increase triggered a backfill/replay that amplified span volume; 2) attribute cardinality rose (lots of big attrs) causing serialization + gzip CPU.

jonas: agree on attrs. we saw similar when debug.user_id tagging leaked into traces last year. serialization cost per-span dominates when batch sizes are small. what is our batch processor config?

eli: current collector config (prod):
```
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 512
    timeout: 5s
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 1s
    limit_mib: 2048
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: https://telemetry-ingest.prod
    compression: gzip
```

maya: notes: send_batch_size=512 is ok, but if average span ~1kb and we have double the span rate, we may be CPU-bound on marshalling/compression. Also retention backfills can cause the exporter to reprocess queued spans.

jonas: two tuning knobs I'd try: increase batch size to 2k (we have memory headroom if memory_limiter allows), and temporarily strip high-cardinality debug tags in the collector (attributes processor). but stripping customer-provided attrs is a product/ops call.

daria: We should consider SDK-side sampling (tail or probabilistic) vs collector. SDK sampling gives customer control and keeps observability parity, but many customers don't upgrade SDKs quickly. collector-based sampling is faster to roll but noisier for customers.

maya: +1. operationally we need a quick mitigation in prod. proposal: 1) enable attributes action=delete for debug.* and request_id-ish keys in collector config, 2) increase batch size to 1024 and raise timeout to 10s, 3) enable gzip if not already (eli shows gzip on somehow). roll this to staging first.

jonas: quick perf note: increasing batch_size reduces per-span overhead but increases memory pressure and export latency. for exporter_export_time_p99=480ms we might be CPU-limited not network-limited; more batching should still help CPU.

infra-bot: alert: retention-change job completed at 10:58 UTC. background reindex started. affected services: telemetry-exporter-*. Estimated additional span volume: +180%.

eli: thanks infra-bot — that matches. so it's a retention-triggered reindex/backfill.

maya: i'll open a staging config patch with attribute trimming and batch_size=1024. can someone run a quick canary against a replica?

deploy-bot: Deployed collector-config v3 to staging (collector-staging-1). CI: green.

jonas: running canary load now (replay script at infra/tools/telemetry-replay). will report p99 CPU and exporter_export_time in ~20m.

(20m later)
jonas: quick numbers from staging: p99 CPU dropped from 92% -> 56% on canary pods, exporter_export_time_p99 dropped 480ms -> 120ms. spans_processed still high but latency much better.

daria: that's encouraging. next discussion: should we make attribute trimming a default during retention/backfill windows? we could add a flag `collector.backfill_mode=true` and have automated attribute pruning during that window.

maya: product/legal note: we need to document exactly what we drop (debug.* etc.) and offer a knob to opt-out for customers who need full fidelity.

eli: action items I got: 
- maya: PR for prod config with attribute deletions + batch_size=1024 + longer timeout
- jonas: run wider canary across eu/us clusters for 24h
- daria: write a short internal note for support/product about what we drop and when

eli: i'll also open a quick RFC for `collector.backfill_mode` to capture the operational semantics and opt-out flow.

maya: thanks — will push PR and ping here when prod rollout is scheduled. :thumbsup:
